Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 1. FIRST CONTACT & PERSONAL IDENTITY
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Are You Ok
- Materials: vocabulary cards, audio, reading handout
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles be and adjectives from Lesson 1.15.
Recycled language: okay, fine, tired.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to this topic?
Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

okay — fine, not bad. Example: I am okay, thank you.
fine — well, in good health. Example: I feel fine today.
tired — needing rest or sleep. Example: I am tired after work.
ill — not well, sick. Example: She is ill and stays at home.
dizzy — feeling that everything turns around. Example: I feel dizzy when I stand up.
pale — with a white face. Example: You look pale.
hurt — to feel pain. Example: My head hurts.
help — to do something useful for someone. Example: Can you help me, please?
rest — to stop working and relax. Example: Sit down and rest.
doctor — a person who treats ill people. Example: The doctor is coming now.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Are you okay?
• I am not feeling well.
• I feel dizzy.
• You look pale.
• Sit down and rest.
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.

Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

Listen and repeat three times.

Grammar focus: Present continuous.
Use the present continuous for things happening now: I am resting. She is not feeling well. Question: Are you okay?
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct sentence.
___ you okay?
Complete the sentence.
Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
Anna is pale and dizzy. She is not feeling well today. She is resting on the sofa and drinking water. Her friend is calling the doctor.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: Are you okay? B: No, I am feeling dizzy. A: You look pale. Sit down and rest. B: Thank you. I am calling the doctor.
Speaking: Pair and group tasks: Roleplay checking on a friend who looks unwell.

• Are you okay?
• I am not feeling well.
• I feel dizzy.
Writing: Write four to five sentences about "Are You Ok" using the target grammar.
